column1: # ALLOC-CLASSES.tsv -- THE CLASS OF EVERY DIRECT ALLOCATION SITE OF THE XPCE KERNEL LIBRARY (DESIGN-PLAN prolog-xpce step 2, the cio 2026-11-16; ENGINE.md 6.2; read by scripts/util_xpce_alloc_census.py).
# A site is a relocation of a built object against malloc, calloc, realloc, strdup or free (readelf -r; the objects are compiled -ffunction-sections, so a site names its function;
# the count is the compiler's, gcc 13.3.0 at -O3 as the recipe builds, and the build's key holds the compiler's version). One row a site, cells split by a tab:
# object (the kernel's path under src, STREAM/ for the oracle's stream file), function, callee, count, class, why. The build refuses a site with no row and a row with no site.
# A CLASS IS DECIDED BY WHO RELEASES THE BLOCK, never by who makes it:
#   KERNEL   the kernel releases it: the object's five names are renamed onto xpce_k_malloc, xpce_k_calloc, xpce_k_realloc, xpce_k_strdup and xpce_k_free (xpce_host.c), which call
#            the kernel's own three slots; a host that fills the slots (SCRIP's binding, the graphics arena) then owns every such block.
#   XOWNED   X or the C library releases or keeps it: it stays libc's.
#   DEFAULT  the kernel's own default slots, which the three slot calls reach while no host fills them.
# NO OBJECT MIXES KERNEL WITH ANOTHER CLASS (each block of the 37 kernel sites was followed to its release, 2026-11-16), so the conversion is of whole objects by objcopy and
# NO PER-SITE CONVERSION IS BUILT: an object that came to mix would refuse the build, and that day the arm is designed. No source line and no copy of a source is changed.
# ONE DEFECT OF THE KERNEL ITSELF, FOR THE BINDING (step 10) TO MEET: img/gifread.c makes its pixel buffer with malloc (line 254, XOWNED: libXpm releases it) and on its error path
# releases the same buffer with pceFree (line 264). While the slots are libc's that is harmless; under a host's allocator it is a libc block handed to the host's free. The
# binding's free and realloc slots therefore answer an address outside the arena's window by libc's own free and realloc (one compare, the window being at a fixed address).
